intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that MEHMO syndrome (MEHMO) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the EIF2S3 gene (300161) on chromosome Xp22.11.

paragraphs.text: DeLozier-Blanchet et al. (1999) described MEHMO as a new syndrome made up of mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity. Skopkova et al. (2017) described MEHMO as a rare X-linked syndrome characterized by profound intellectual disability, epilepsy, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity. They linked it to mutations in EIF2S3, which encodes the gamma subunit of translation initiation factor eIF2. They placed it among disorders of translation initiation and the integrated stress response.

paragraphs.text: Borck et al. (2012) described a family of Moroccan Jewish ancestry in the maternal line. In this family, 3 males had an X-linked intellectual disability syndrome with moderate-to-severe intellectual disability, microcephaly, short stature, and facial dysmorphism. Individual features differed among the 3 males. Patient III:1 had cleft lip and palate and behavioral impairment, patient III:2 had generalized seizures, and patient II:3 had postpubertal microgenitalism and obesity. Brain MRI showed a thin corpus callosum and enlarged lateral ventricles. The parents I.1 and I.2 were first cousins.

paragraphs.text: Skopkova et al. (2017) reported a Slovak boy (family 1) born to nonconsanguineous parents. Microcephaly was detected prenatally. At birth he had micropenis, cryptorchidism, and peripheral hypertonia. Drug-resistant partial complex seizures began at 4 months. He went on to have severe developmental delay and central obesity, and non-autoimmune insulin-treated diabetes was diagnosed at 10 months. His dysmorphic features included full cheeks, large ears, downturned corners of the mouth, epiblepharon, tapered fingers, and talipes. Brain MRI showed delayed myelination that progressed with acute demyelinating changes and cerebral atrophy. Muscle biopsy showed abnormal mitochondria. His seizures and diabetes control worsened during infections. At 5 years his height was -5 SD and his head circumference was -8.4 SD.

His dysmorphic features included facial telangiectasias, edematous hands and feet, and bilateral talipes. Diabetes was diagnosed at 6 months after a ketoacidotic crisis. He died at 2 years with refractory seizures. Female carriers in the family were unaffected.

paragraphs.text: Borck et al. (2012) studied the 3 affected males of a Moroccan Jewish family with X-linked intellectual disability and microcephaly. Borck et al. (2012) sequenced all 12 exons of EIF2S3 in 60 individuals from families with unspecific, potentially X-linked intellectual disability and found no additional mutations. They took this to suggest that EIF2S3 mutations confer a specific phenotype. Borck et al. (2012) also noted an EIF2S3 missense variant, c.451G-C (V151L), previously reported in an X-linked intellectual disability resequencing project. The variant was absent from SNP databases and predicted to be damaging. The orthologous yeast mutation (V210L) lies near the Met-tRNAi binding site and caused defects in growth, GCN4 expression, and start site selection.

paragraphs.text: Skopkova et al. (2017) studied affected males from 3 families with MEHMO syndrome: 2 Slovak families and the German family originally reported by Steinmüller et al. (1998). Whole-exome or X-chromosome exome sequencing identified the same hemizygous 4-bp deletion in the last exon of EIF2S3 (c.1394_1397delTCAA). The deletion causes a frameshift (ile465serfsTer4) that replaces the last 8 amino acids with 3 different ones. It segregated with the disease, was absent from dbSNP and ExAC, and had a CADD score of 35. Trio exome sequencing in the more mildly affected boy from family 4 identified a hemizygous c.324T-A transversion in EIF2S3, resulting in a ser108-to-arg (S108R) substitution, which he inherited from his healthy mother. Ser108 is conserved down to Drosophila, and the variant was absent from dbSNP and ExAC, with a CADD score of 24. However, the equivalent yeast mutation had no effect, and the healthy brother could not be tested. The authors therefore classified S108R as a variant of unknown significance.

paragraphs.text: Skopkova et al. (2017) modeled the ile465serfsTer4 mutation in a yeast/human eIF2-gamma chimera. The mutant chimera was expressed at normal protein levels but caused slow growth, which was worse at 37 degrees C. It derepressed GCN4-lacZ expression nearly 3-fold and doubled the UUG/AUG initiation ratio. These effects were comparable to those of the X-linked intellectual disability-associated Val281Thr mutation and indicated that the C-terminal mutation impairs eIF2 function. Patient fibroblasts produced the C-terminally truncated eIF2-gamma protein. In fibroblasts from a family 3 patient, DDIT3 transcript levels were 2.5-fold higher than in controls and CHOP protein was also elevated, indicating activation of the integrated stress response. Skopkova et al. (2017) proposed that EIF2S3 mutations, like mutations in the EIF2B genes and PPP1R15B, reduce the activity or availability of the eIF2 ternary complex. They suggested that this leads to insufficient protein synthesis and chronically elevated ATF4 and CHOP, which cause apoptosis. They also noted that patient 1's condition worsened markedly during illness, as in vanishing white matter disease.

paragraphs.text: Skopkova et al. (2017) studied affected males with MEHMO syndrome from 3 families: 2 Slovak families and the German family originally reported by Steinmüller et al. (1998). Whole-exome or X-chromosome exome sequencing identified the same hemizygous c.1394_1397delTCAA deletion in the last exon of EIF2S3. The deletion causes a frameshift (ile465serfsTer4) that replaces the last 8 amino acids with 3 different ones. It segregated with the disease, was absent from dbSNP and ExAC, and had a CADD score of 35. A yeast/human eIF2-gamma chimera carrying the mutation caused slow growth, derepressed GCN4-lacZ expression nearly 3-fold, and doubled the UUG/AUG initiation ratio. Patient fibroblasts produced the truncated protein and showed elevated DDIT3 transcript and CHOP protein levels, indicating activation of the integrated stress response. The 3 families reported no common ancestors. Haplotype comparison suggested a founder effect with distant relatedness. All 4 index patients with this mutation had full MEHMO syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Gregory et al. (2019) studied 3 affected males from a white European family with hypopituitarism and glucose dysregulation: monozygotic twins and their maternal cousin. X-exome sequencing identified a hemizygous c.1294C-T transition in the EIF2S3 gene, resulting in a pro432-to-ser (P432S) substitution at a highly conserved residue in the C-terminal domain of eIF2-gamma. The variant was inherited from the boys' heterozygous mothers, who were sisters, and segregated in an X-linked recessive manner over 3 generations. It was absent from ExAC and gnomAD. In yeast, the equivalent P490S mutation caused a modest (about 1.7-fold) significant increase in GCN4-lacZ expression and increased UUG start codon initiation. The patients did not have the microcephaly, epilepsy, and obesity of classic MEHMO syndrome. The authors proposed that the milder loss of function of P432S produces a distinct phenotype.
